- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above prior high or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive move, model delays correction; add a 1–2 day lag in downward adjustment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast > 85 and true < 75, apply 10–15% downward bias for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model overestimates volatility; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “tail risk” overfitting: if sentiment shows increasing pessimism, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day for 3 days before true drop.
